sources.claim: Fake or AI-generated reviews and testimonials that misrepresent real experiences are deceptive; the FTC has rules and guidance against fake reviews. The course teaches the principle (do not invent or buy reviews), not the rule's penalty details.

sections.skill: Keep ad claims truthful and handle complaints well

questions.prompt: Which claim is misleading?

choices.text: "Ships in 3 days" when that is the usual time

questions.intro: Advertising must be TRUTHFUL and not misleading, and claims that need proof must be supported before they are made. This includes prices ("from 20 dollars" must be available), comparisons ("cheaper than X" must be accurate), environmental claims ("eco-friendly"), and fake urgency ("only 2 left" when there are 200). Fake reviews and testimonials are deceptive. When customers COMPLAIN, respond quickly and calmly, find out what happened, fix what you can, and keep a record. Complaints often show where to improve.

questions.prompt: An ad is like what?
questions.intro: If a lemonade stand sign says "Fresh squeezed, 1 dollar," customers expect fresh juice for a dollar. If it is powdered mix for 2 dollars, they feel tricked, even if it tastes fine. An ad is a promise on a sign. And when someone complains, listening calmly is like checking whether your lemonade really was what the sign said.
